items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee discusses Mel Lewis in the context of answering a question about drummers in general and references 'he found Mel', but does not explicitly state a personal or professional relationship between himself (Slide Hampton) and Mel Lewis.

ctx.x: The reason I ask that is because I think of Mel Lewis as a prototypical big-band drummer, and I want to ask you how important the drummers are that play in your highly arranged scenarios, and what you want from them, what you ask of them, how you get what you need from them?

If they’re not qualified, you can’t get what you need from them. It has to be somebody that’s qualified, because the drummer’s responsibility is great. That means that he has a lot of experience in playing different kinds of music, he’s a sensitive person, and he wants to make the musical result whatever you want it to be. Often, drummers are not

people that you can get to participate in things like that that easily, because they have a lot of ego and they have a lot of insecurities and things. So I guess it was – when he found Mel, it was probably, for him – was a real plus.
